solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lucky devil on a trip abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters of these words are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist calls the devil's own luck on a foreign holiday a stroke of good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' looks like part of the holiday picture but signals the rearrangement of DEVILONATRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something providential happens as if by divine provision, so it is fortunate or lucky.

clue.text: Left one's husband by bar to circulate

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pub is placed beside the other pieces

parts.note: a bar is a pub
one's read as one is gives I and IS
H is the abbreviation for husband in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a spouse at the pub in order to get around socially.
explanation.definitionFit: To publish a story is to make it public, to circulate it widely.

clue.text: Stones featuring old sidekick Watts' finale

parts.note: a sidekick is a pal or companion

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter, here taken from the name Watts

explanation.surface: Gems featuring in the act of an old comic's sidekick called Watts.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are precious gemstones, and stones is a common word for gems.

clue.text: Unfaithful siren, nice in a bad way

indicators.note: in a bad way suggests something wrecked or out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seductive woman who is pleasant in a wicked manner proves untrue to her lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An insincere person does not mean what they say, so is false or unfaithful to their word.

clue.text: The woman's commonly spoken mistakes

indicators.note: commonly spoken means said aloud in a working-class accent that drops the initial H

parts.note: the woman's means belonging to her, which is hers

explanation.surface: A woman's errors are discussed in everyday speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the H in common British speech turns HERS into 'ERS, which sounds the same as ERRS.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so the verb form errs means makes mistakes.

clue.text: Pie hasn't splattered actor

indicators.note: splattered suggests something smashed apart and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The custard pie thrown at a performer has missed its target.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in hasn't is ignored, leaving PIEHASNT to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is a stage performer, named after Thespis, the legendary first Greek actor.

clue.text: Awfully long, awful massacre often starts battle

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of the preceding words are taken

explanation.surface: A dreadful, drawn-out slaughter is often how fighting begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo (1836) was a famous siege in Texas, ending in a massacre of its defenders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was a famous engagement of the Texas Revolution, so it is an example of a battle.

clue.text: The setter's raised with obedience outside home

indicators.note: outside says the word for obedience goes around the other piece

parts.note: obedience is taken as docile, the quality of being easily led

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: the setter's is read as the setter is, which the setter would say as I'm

explanation.surface: A crossword setter describes being brought up in a well-behaved household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is the crossword setter saying 'I'm'; in a down clue 'raised' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is the place where someone lives, a formal word for home.

clue.text: Consumed case of raspberries eating fine dessert

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the letter for fine goes inside

parts.note: consumed means ate
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, here the first and last of raspberries

explanation.surface: Someone has eaten a punnet of raspberries with a fine pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' keeps only the outer letters of raspberries; 'eating' then puts the F inside the combined consumed-plus-case run.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is informal British for the pudding course that follows the main meal.

clue.text: Supporter's order unfinished in bar

parts.note: a bra is a supporter, and the possessive adds S

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a series is an order or sequence of things

explanation.surface: An underwear order is left incomplete inside a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant and bar.

clue.text: Cold sponge, toe to head

indicators.note: toe to head means the final letter is moved to the front

parts.note: a loofa is a bath sponge made from a dried gourd

explanation.surface: Someone scrubs themselves with a bath sponge from foot to head.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the last A of LOOFA to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aloof person is distant and unfriendly, which is cold in manner.

clue.text: Inside restrains a neurotic lunatic

indicators.note: inside says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Indoors, someone holds back an anxious madman.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of 'restrains' and continues through 'a neurotic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic as an adjective means mad, the same as insane.

clue.text: Facing work with flower plot

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
a flower is a river, something that flows, here the Italian river Po
a plot of land is a site

explanation.surface: A gardening job involves a bed of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' as a river (one that flows) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite means across from, so facing something in position.

clue.text: Better to accept advice finally from doctor

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: better in health is haler, the comparative of hale

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of advice is used

explanation.surface: It is wiser to follow the last piece of guidance from your GP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a verb or 'superior'; here it is HALER, healthier.
explanation.definitionFit: A healer is one who cures the sick, a general word for a doctor.

clue.text: Outrage seeing altar boy oddly on town

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above the next piece
oddly means the odd-placed letters of altar boy are taken

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A scandal involving a choirboy in the local town.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is a shockingly cruel act, an outrage.

clue.text: Turn small pan over for vegetables

indicators.note: over means the whole lot is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to turn is to spin
to pan is to criticise, to rap

explanation.surface: Flip the little saucepan to get the root veg out.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are pale root vegetables related to the carrot.

clue.text: Marine's a force in extreme environment

indicators.note: environment means surroundings, so the word for extreme surrounds the rest

parts.note: searing heat is extreme, so searing means intense
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A Royal Marine is a fighting force in the harshest conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafaring as an adjective means relating to the sea, as marine does.

clue.text: Animal act taking time with tailless cat

indicators.note: taking means the word for act holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a play is a dramatic act or performance

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A creature performs a trick for a while with a cat that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is an egg-laying Australian mammal, so an animal.

clue.text: Appearance by Queen lavishly ends earlier

indicators.note: by means alongside, so the last pieces follow

parts.note: form is shape or appearance
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen

indicators.note: ends means the first and last letters of lavishly

explanation.surface: The monarch dressing lavishly finishes sooner.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly means at an earlier time, previously.

clue.text: Starves consuming last of sustenance? Hardly!

definitions.text: Starves consuming last of sustenance? Hardly!

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the word for starves holds the letter

parts.note: starves means goes without food, fasts

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of sustenance

explanation.surface: Someone going hungry eats a final bite of food, or not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly!' says the answer is the opposite of starving: eating lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasts are lavish meals, the very opposite of fasting.

clue.text: Animals issued with large back of humps

parts.note: issued means came out or came forth
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of humps

explanation.surface: Creatures emerge, with a large hump on their backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels are humped desert mammals, so examples of animals.

clue.text: Belonging to 'chosen', a Tory politician

indicators.note: Belonging to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Conservative belongs to the elite chosen to govern.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: Literal account given by minister

indicators.note: given by means placed alongside the next piece

parts.note: a curate is a junior Anglican clergyman, a minister

explanation.surface: A vicar provides a word-for-word report.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal rendering is exact, so accurate to the original.

clue.text: Drink followed by endless pole dance

indicators.note: followed by means the next piece comes after

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a bar is a pole or rod

explanation.surface: A drink is followed by an all-night routine on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a lively Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Shameless, to need love before noon, in short

indicators.note: before means the preceding pieces come ahead of the last one

parts.note: need means want
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Wanting romance before midday is brazen, briefly put.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanton means immoral or unrestrained, without shame.

clue.text: Idiot swallowing Sun's spin

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for idiot takes the letter inside

parts.note: a twit is an idiot
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A fool falls for the tabloid's slant on a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; here Sun is Sunday, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a spin or rotation, as in giving something a turn.

clue.text: Area covering Thailand formerly — mass in excess?

definitions.text: Area covering Thailand formerly — mass in excess?

indicators.note: in excess means surplus, so this letter is removed

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand
M is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A region once including Siam has too much bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the continent: it covers Thailand and is vast.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a vast region that includes Thailand.

clue.text: Bear, Mohawk's original symbol

parts.note: to bear is to carry, tote

indicators.note: original means the first letter of Mohawk's

explanation.surface: A bear is the emblem of a Native American tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or symbol of a clan, often an animal.

clue.text: Nuisance embracing single girl upset killjoy

indicators.note: embracing means the word for nuisance goes around the rest

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word for girl is read backwards

parts.note: miss is a word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: An annoying person hugs a lone woman who becomes distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimist always expects the worst, so dampens fun like a killjoy.

clue.text: Bloke's scream approaching unending stretch for killing

indicators.note: approaching means coming up to the next piece

parts.note: a bloke is a man, and the possessive adds S
a scream is something hilarious, a laugh

indicators.note: unending means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a term is a stretch of time, such as a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A man's shriek as his long prison term nears its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is unlawful killing without intent to murder.
